steps.title: Prepare fluorescein staining solution
steps.instruction: Just before use, add 1 µL of 10 mM fluorescein (dissolved in ethanol treated with molecular sieves) to ultrapure water and bring the volume up to ≤1 mL to obtain a 10 µM fluorescein staining solution.

steps.title: Excise leaf disk
steps.instruction: Use a 2.0 mm diameter hole puncher to cut a leaf disk from an Arabidopsis thaliana leaf.

steps.title: Load leaf disk into syringe
steps.instruction: Add 2–5 mL ultrapure water to a disposable 10 mL syringe, place the leaf disk inside with tweezers, insert the plunger, and avoid spilling water from the syringe top.

steps.title: Deaerate leaf disk
steps.instruction: Hold the syringe top and repeatedly pull the plunger to draw water through the leaf disk; repeat several times until the leaf disk appears deaerated.

steps.title: Transfer leaf disk to staining tube
steps.instruction: Using tweezers, move the deaerated leaf disk into a 1.5 mL microtube containing 1 mL of the 10 µM fluorescein solution and gently invert the tube several times to fully immerse the disk.

steps.title: Incubate staining
steps.instruction: Incubate the leaf disk for 10 min, performing one or two gentle inversions of the microtube during the incubation to ensure even staining.

steps.title: Mount leaf disk on slide
steps.instruction: Moisten a super‑frost slide glass with ultrapure water, place the stained leaf disk onto the slide without rinsing, and cover with a 20 × 50 mm cover glass (thickness 0.16–0.19 mm).

steps.title: Image leaf disk by confocal microscopy
steps.instruction: Place the slide on a Leica TCS SP8X confocal microscope and acquire fluorescence using the following settings: White Light Laser intensity 21% (30% of the 70% power WLL), objective HC PL APO 63×/1.20 W CORR CS2 water‑immersion, scan format 100 Hz/512 × 512 pixels, detector HyD (or PMT), excitation 488 nm, emission 500–550 nm for fluorescein and 680–720 nm for chlorophyll, time gating off (0.5–1.2 ns).
